# Wald-Q4B v1.1

> Open-weight 4B decision model. Given a state and typed questions (choice, yes/no, score), it returns a calibrated probability for every option through a Jev-compatible `POST /v1/systemone` API. Built on Qwen3.5-4B-Base; Apache-2.0 weights and serving code; self-hosted on one NVIDIA GPU with vLLM. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by TypeSafe AI.

Key facts:
- Hugging Face repository: Harry19081/Wald-4B (current release tag `v1.1`; earlier name Wald-4B). GitHub: Harry19081/wald-4b.
- Uses: tool selection, agent routing, classification, deciding whether to ask the user a clarifying question.
- Effort levels: `none` (one pass, no generated tokens), `low`, `medium`, `high` (default), `high-k2`…`high-k8`.
- JevBench public set (231 items), effort `none`: 203/231, ECE 0.041, p50 33 ms / p95 168 ms on one RTX PRO 6000. Self-scored with JevBench's harness; the public items were a development scoreboard, not held out. Leaderboard row requested in fstandhartinger/jevbench issue #146.
- Decision Index 0.2.1 complete suite, effort `high`: 54.59 balanced-skill index. Author-run; submission apolinario/decision-index PR #30 awaits maintainer validation.
